name: 积分商城
description: Points shop, auctions and blind boxes. Migrated out of api/modules/marketplace/**. Adopts the four pre-existing tables it writes (auctions, blind_boxes, shop_items, redemption_tickets) rather than renaming them, because SELECT * rows are returned straight through to the frontend and api/modules/admin/admin.repository.ts deletes shop_items and redemption_tickets by legacy name in its teacher/student cascade. Student points move through classroom.public: spends and refunds use transferStudentCredits (available balance only, exactly what the pre-migration spendStudentPoints and the raw refund UPDATE did) while the blind-box consolation uses adjustPoints (both balances, exactly what addStudentPoints did).

data._adopted_note: All four keep their legacy names: the rows are the JSON contract (price, stock, is_active, teacher_id, is_holiday_limited, highest_bidder_id, code ...) and admin.repository.ts still deletes shop_items/redemption_tickets by name in its teacher/student cascade. auctions and blind_boxes are marketplace-only. shop_items and redemption_tickets are SHARED with the not-yet-migrated engagement domain (engagement.service.ts:148-173 reads shop_items and updates redemption_tickets.status; :439 inserts a redemption ticket). They are adopted here because this plugin WRITES both (shop CRUD, stock decrement, ticket issue) and `ctx.db` refuses a write to a table that is only declared in `data.reads` - a reads-only declaration would make five statements throw TableOwnershipError in every non-production boot. Ownership of these two is therefore transitional and must be re-decided when engagement migrates (either engagement routes its writes through a marketplace port, or the declaration moves).
data._cleanup_note: P4.3b.14: marketplace is the single cleanup owner of `shop_items` and `redemption_tickets` for `DELETE /api/admin/users/:id`, ported from admin.repository.ts:472 (tickets by student) and :554 (shop items by teacher). `redemption_tickets` is the guardrail's documented SHARED_WRITE_TABLES exception - engagement also writes it - but the cleanup registry accepts exactly ONE owner per table and rejects a second registration, so the two plugins cannot both claim it. Marketplace owns it because the table's lifecycle and CRUD live here; engagement only issues prizes, and its manifest must not register a rule naming this table (doing so fails engagement's setup()). The write-sharing itself is still open debt, recorded in marketplace's and engagement's `_adopted_note`/`_known_debt`.
data._known_debt: 1. AUTHORIZATION, closed this round: all sixteen `/api/shop` routes were reachable with no credential at all, and the money paths took `studentId` from the request body, so an anonymous caller could spend another student's points. Every route now resolves the caller from the kernel's verified request context (401 `未登录或登录已过期` before any validation message; 403 `无权限执行该操作` for a known caller without the role) via `src/marketplace.authorization.ts`, and `studentActorId` returns `Actor.studentId` (the `students` row) instead of the old conflation with `Actor.userId` (the login row). Item/auction/blind-box administration is teacher/admin, buying is student-self, and the shop read is scoped to the caller's own shelf: a student's class teacher's active items, a teacher's own items, everything for admin - it used to answer the whole table whenever `?studentId=` was omitted. `PUT /api/shop/:id`(+`/status`) checks `shop_items.teacher_id` against the actor. The `auth: "actor"` declarations in `provides.routes` below were aspirational until this round; they are now accurate. 2. NOT done, deliberately: the routes are role-gated, not capability-gated - no `ctx.permissions` declaration (e.g. `marketplace.purchase`) exists yet, and the matrix rules on roles, so inventing a capability here would change behaviour beyond the ruling. 3. `GET /api/shop/auctions` cannot be narrowed to the matrix's `student/teacher（本班）`: `auctions` carries no class or teacher column (the row IS the JSON contract), so the gate is the role half only. Adding the column is a coordinated frontend change. 4. DELIBERATE DEVIATION on `GET /api/shop/blind_boxes`: the matrix's role column reads teacher/admin, but the deployed student shop page reads this route (`useStudentShopData` -> `getStudentItems()` + `getBlindBoxes()` in one `Promise.all`), so the student role is admitted and the read is *scoped* instead of refused - staff get every box (management listing, inactive included), a student gets the active ones after the `enable_auction_blind_box` gate. The anonymous hole the matrix's note describes ("sees every row including the ended ones") is closed either way. 5. The three money paths still pass `actorId: 0` into `classroom.public.transferStudentCredits`/`adjustPoints`, exactly as the pre-migration code did, so the ledger row does not name the spender; the actor is now known at the boundary and threading it through is a separate, reviewable change.
